n: The heading says David sang this after the Lord rescued him from Saul and all his enemies. Nearly the same song appears in 2 Samuel 22. It opens with a deeply personal “I love you, Lord.”

f.g: A rare, tender Hebrew word for love, related to the word for womb or compassion.

n: David piles up images of protection: rock, fortress, deliverer, shield, horn, and high tower. God is every kind of safety at once.

f.g: A small shield.
The horn symbolizes strength; Zacharias used this phrase of Jesus.

n: He calls on the Lord, who deserves praise, and is saved from his enemies.
The cords of death wrapped around him, and torrents of destruction terrified him.

f.g: Better “the cords of death” — death pictured as a hunter’s ropes.
Torrents of destruction (Hebrew belial, worthlessness or ruin).

n: The ropes of the grave surrounded him; the snares of death confronted him.

f.g: Hebrew sheol — the grave.
Came to meet, confronted.

n: In distress he cried to God, and God heard him from his temple — his heavenly dwelling.

f.w: he heard my voice out of his temple

n: God’s response is pictured as a cosmic storm: the earth quakes and mountains shake because he is angry at what was done to his servant.
Smoke rises from his nostrils and devouring fire from his mouth — poetic images of God’s fierce intervention.
He parts the heavens and comes down, with dark clouds under his feet.

f.w: He bowed the heavens also, and came down

n: He rides on a cherub and soars on the wings of the wind.

f.g: A winged heavenly being, guardian of God’s holy presence.

n: He wraps himself in darkness, with dark rain clouds as his canopy.

f.g: A canopy or tent.

f.w: He made darkness his secret place

n: Out of the brightness before him, clouds burst with hail and lightning.

f.g: Lightning bolts.

n: The Lord thunders from heaven; the Most High’s voice sounds amid hail and fiery bolts.
He shoots his arrows — lightning — and scatters the enemy in confusion.

f.g: Threw into panic, routed.

n: At his rebuke the sea bed is exposed and the foundations of the world laid bare — echoing the Red Sea crossing.

f.w: the channels of waters were seen

f.g: Uncovered, laid bare.

n: God reached down from above, took hold of David, and drew him out of deep waters — as Moses (whose name means “drawn out”) was drawn from water.

f.w: he drew me out of many waters

n: God rescued him from a powerful enemy — probably Saul — and from foes too strong for him.
They attacked him on his worst day, but the Lord was his support.

f.g: Support, prop.

n: God brought him into a wide-open place of freedom and rescued him because he delighted in him.

f.g: Spaciousness — freedom from confinement and distress.

n: The Lord rewarded him according to his righteousness and clean hands. David is speaking of his loyalty to God against Saul, not claiming lifelong perfection.
He kept the Lord’s ways and did not turn away from his God.

f.w: have not wickedly departed from my God

n: All God’s laws were before him, and he didn’t set aside his decrees.

f.g: Decrees, ordinances.

n: He was blameless before God and kept himself from sin.

f.g: Blameless, whole-hearted — the same word used of Noah and Job.

n: So the Lord repaid him according to his righteousness — the clean hands God himself saw.

f.g: As God sees it, not merely as people judge.

n: God responds in kind: to the faithful he shows faithfulness, to the blameless he shows himself blameless.

f.w: With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful

n: To the pure he shows himself pure, but to the crooked he shows himself shrewd.

f.g: Perverse, crooked, twisted.

n: He saves the humble but brings down those with proud looks.
The Lord keeps David’s lamp burning and turns his darkness into light.

f.g: Keep my lamp burning — preserve my life and line.

n: With God’s help he can charge an army troop and leap over a city wall.

f.w: I have run through a troop
f.g: Or “crushed a troop.”

n: God’s way is perfect, his word proven true. He shields all who take refuge in him.

f.w: the word of the LORD is tried
f.g: Refined, tested and proven.

n: Who is God except the Lord? Who is a rock besides our God?

f.w: who is a rock save our God?

n: God arms him with strength and makes his path secure.

f.g: Wraps strength around me like a belt.

n: He makes David’s feet as nimble as a deer’s, able to stand on the heights.

f.g: The sure-footed feet of a deer.

n: He trains David’s hands for battle so he can bend a bronze bow.

f.g: A bow of bronze — hard to draw.

n: God gives him the shield of salvation, upholds him, and makes him great by stooping down to help.

f.w: thy gentleness hath made me great
f.g: Literally “your humility” or “your stooping down” — God’s condescension lifts David up.

n: God widened the path under him so his ankles wouldn’t give way.

f.g: Gave me a broad, secure path.

n: David pursued his enemies and did not turn back until they were finished.

f.w: neither did I turn again till they were consumed

n: He struck them down so they couldn’t rise; they fell beneath his feet.

f.w: they are fallen under my feet

n: God armed him for battle and humbled his attackers.

f.w: girded me with strength unto the battle

n: God made his enemies turn their backs in flight, and he destroyed those who hated him.

f.w: given me the necks of mine enemies
f.g: Made them turn and flee, or placed his foot on their necks — a sign of victory.

n: They cried for help, even to the Lord, but no one saved them — they had not sought him before.

f.w: even unto the LORD, but he answered them not

n: He ground them fine as dust in the wind and trampled them like mud in the streets.

f.w: as the dust before the wind

n: God rescued him from attacks by the people and made him head of nations; foreign peoples now serve him.

f.g: Ruler over foreign nations.

n: As soon as they hear of him they obey; foreigners come cringing to him.

f.g: Foreigners will feign obedience or come cringing.

n: Foreigners lose heart and come trembling out of their fortresses.

f.g: Strongholds, fortresses.

n: The Lord lives! Praise to my Rock! Exalted be the God who saves me.
It is God who avenges David and subdues nations under him.

f.w: It is God that avengeth me

n: He rescues David from his enemies, exalts him above his attackers, and delivers him from violent men.

f.g: Possibly Saul, or any violent foe.

n: So David will praise God among the nations. Paul quotes this verse to show that the gospel was meant for Gentiles too.

f.w: will I give thanks unto thee, O LORD, among the heathen

n: God gives great victories to his king and shows covenant love to his anointed, David, and his descendants forever — a promise fulfilled ultimately in Christ, the Son of David.

f.g: Messiah — the anointed king.

f.w: to David, and to his seed for evermore
